clue.text: Ineffectual type makes fortune importing Edam, surprisingly

indicators.note: something turning out surprisingly has not gone as arranged, so these letters come out in an unexpected order
to import is to bring goods inside, so one word takes the other into its middle

blocks.note: fortune, good or bad, is luck
the Dutch cheese, taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gambler strikes it rich after a lucky deal involving a Dutch cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lame duck' was first stock-exchange slang for a trader who could not pay their debts, which suits the surface's talk of fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A lame duck is an idiom for a weak or ineffective person, such as an official who has lost power.

clue.text: The French holding one sailor on line responsible

indicators.note: holding means gripping something within, so the outer word wraps the others

blocks.note: le is French for the
the Roman numeral for one
AB is an able-bodied seaman
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A French seaman is held to account for something on a shipping line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just strings the sailor and the line together inside LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being liable means being legally answerable for something, which is the same as being responsible.

clue.text: Mistress's ire got out of control in this familiar song

indicators.note: something out of control runs wild, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lover's fury boils over, as told in a well-known ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Otis Regrets is a Cole Porter song in which a society woman shoots her faithless lover, so the surface fits the song's story.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Otis Regrets is a well-known Cole Porter song from 1934, recorded by many singers.

clue.text: What may help to make things clearer along the way?

definitions.text: What may help to make things clearer along the way?

blocks.clueFragment: What may help to make things clearer along the way?
blocks.note: surface reading: some aid to understanding as a process goes on

blocks.clueFragment: What may help to make things clearer along the way?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a car control that lowers the headlights so oncoming drivers on the road can see

explanation.walkthrough: 'Along the way' is literal: on the road. Lowering your headlight beam stops dazzling oncoming drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip switch is the vehicle control that dips headlights from full beam, keeping other motorists' view unobstructed.

clue.text: Appeal to prisoner snatching the whole lot

indicators.note: snatching means grabbing hold of, so the first word clutches the second inside it

blocks.note: con is slang for a convict
the whole lot is all of it

explanation.surface: A jailbird grabs everything and pleads with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on someone for help is to make a request or plea to them, which is appealing to them.

clue.text: Foreign correspondent?

blocks.note: surface reading: a journalist posted abroad to report the news
setter's reading: someone overseas you exchange friendly letters with

explanation.walkthrough: A foreign correspondent is usually a reporter; here it is just a person abroad who writes to you.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen pal is a friend, often living in another country, with whom one regularly exchanges letters.

clue.text: English spring evident in Surrey town

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a spring of water is a well

explanation.surface: An English water source can be seen in a commuter town.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south-west of London. Ewell really was named after its spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewell is a town in the county of Surrey, near Epsom, on the southern edge of Greater London.

clue.text: Game, Pinner scout's playing with her

indicators.note: playing about means moving around freely, so these letters move into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written to be rearranged; Pinner is a suburb of north-west London
taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy scout from Pinner joins a girl in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Puss in the corner is a traditional children's game in which players dash between corners while one tries to steal a spot.

clue.text: Did she make a stack during the war?

definitions.text: Did she make a stack during the war?

blocks.clueFragment: Did she make a stack during the war?
blocks.note: surface reading: asking whether some woman made a fortune in wartime

blocks.clueFragment: Did she make a stack during the war?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a woman doing farm work in wartime, building haystacks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a stack' sounds like slang for earning lots of money; here it is a literal hay or corn stack. The Women's Land Army sent women to work on British farms in both World Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: A land girl was a woman recruited to agricultural labour during the World Wars, replacing men called up to fight.

clue.text: Reflective attitude adopted by a Greek writer

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the wrong way round, so this word is read backwards
being adopted by someone means joining them, so one piece attaches to the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a pose is an attitude struck for effect

explanation.surface: A thoughtful stance taken up by an ancient Greek author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflective' looks like a description of a pensive attitude, but it means the word is mirrored.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek storyteller credited with the famous collection of animal fables.

clue.text: Poor devil in winter at a seaside resort?

blocks.note: poor in quality or spirits is low
to devil food is to season it with hot spices

explanation.surface: Some wretched creature spends the cold months at a deserted beach town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devil' reads as a noun for a wretch, but it is the cooking verb meaning to spice up. The question mark flags that winter is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Resorts call the quiet off-peak months, when few visitors come and prices drop, their low season.

clue.text: Wrote, worried about onset of this type of decay

indicators.note: a worried thing is shaken about, as a dog worries a bone, so these letters get jumbled
the onset is the beginning, so only the first letter of the following word is kept
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written to be rearranged
the first letter of this

explanation.surface: Someone anxiously wrote a report on a kind of decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrote, worried' reads as a writer fretting, but worried is the signal to jumble. 'this' points both to the letter and to the answer as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet rot is a fungal decay that attacks damp timber in buildings, a particular form of rot.

clue.text: Took longish walk foolishly? That's rich, coming from you!

indicators.note: doing something foolishly means doing it without sense, so the letters lose their sensible order

blocks.note: taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who wandered off on a long ramble is mocked by a companion for a hypocritical remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's rich' is the sarcastic retort to a hypocrite, not a comment about money.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idiomatic retorts accusing a speaker of hypocrisy, criticising others for faults they share.

clue.text: One entering large order

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: fat means large in size
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single item gets into a big list of instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: A fiat is an authoritative decree, from the Latin for 'let it be done'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is a formal command or decree issued by someone in authority, which is an order.

clue.text: Guide European celebrity

blocks.note: a Pole is a person from Poland
a celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: A famous figure from the continent shows tourists around.
explanation.definitionFit: The pole star stays fixed in the northern sky and has long served navigators as a guide; figuratively, any guiding principle.

clue.text: What'll help to make jockeys placid?

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: the going is the state of a racecourse, and easy ground helps riders
second meaning: relaxed and calm in temperament

explanation.surface: Something that keeps race riders calm.
explanation.walkthrough: In horse racing 'the going' is the condition of the turf, so easy going suits the jockeys.
explanation.definitionFit: An easygoing person is relaxed and tolerant, not easily upset, which is what placid means.

clue.text: Upset girl, say

blocks.note: Ina is a girl's name
to say something is to state it

explanation.surface: A distressed young woman, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the usual 'for example' signal, but it is the verb meaning to declare.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a state is an idiom for being agitated or anxious, which is being upset.

clue.text: Key member with resolve

blocks.note: a member is a limb, such as a leg
to resolve a matter is to end it

explanation.surface: An important club member who shows determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like an adjective meaning important, but it is the noun for a map's explanatory table.
explanation.definitionFit: The legend on a map or chart is the explanatory key to its symbols.

clue.text: Noah and rest adrift in large body of water

indicators.note: something adrift has lost its moorings and wanders loose, so these letters float out of place

blocks.note: taken as written to be rearranged
taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Noah and the others on the ark float aimlessly over the flood waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply joins the two words of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Sea is the stretch of the Atlantic between Britain and mainland Europe, a large body of water.

clue.text: Get rid of outhouse

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to cast off, as a snake does its skin
second meaning: a noun, a small outbuilding in the garden

explanation.surface: An instruction to demolish the outbuilding at the bottom of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to discard or lose something, and the noun is a simple hut used for storage.

clue.text: I go astray in SA mountain range

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the first pieces sit inside the letters given

blocks.note: taken as written
to err is to stray from the right path
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hiker gets lost in South African peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: SA looks like South Africa but is just the two letters taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged chain of mountains, a Spanish word used in many place names.

clue.text: Make a short journey after tedious rehearsal

indicators.note: after means coming later in sequence, so the first-named piece follows the second

blocks.note: a dry speech or book is tedious
a run is a quick trip, as in a run to the shops

explanation.surface: Popping out for a quick trip after a boring practice session.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry run is a trial performance or practice before the real event, which is a rehearsal.

clue.text: An excursion is their suggestion, possibly

indicators.note: possibly hints at one of several arrangements, so the letters may be put together another way

blocks.note: taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Somebody else proposed this outing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of 'their suggestion' supplies exactly the fifteen letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sightseeing tour is a trip taken to visit attractions, a typical example of an excursion.

clue.text: Find the start of the watercourse

indicators.note: the start of a word is its beginning, so just its first letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of the
a race is a channel of water, as in a millrace

explanation.surface: Discovering where a river rises.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a river's source; in fact 'the start of' takes one letter. A millrace is the channel feeding a waterwheel.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace something is to locate or track it down, so it can mean find.

clue.text: Boy, unusually relaxed about one

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so these letters are not in their normal order
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written to be rearranged
an is the indefinite article, meaning one, as in 'an apple'

explanation.surface: A lad is surprisingly laid-back about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander is a common male first name, so it can stand for a boy in crossword terms.

clue.text: Private meal - daughter excluded

indicators.note: excluded means left out, so the named letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: dinner is a meal
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: An intimate supper to which the daughter was not invited.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner feelings or thoughts are personal ones kept hidden from others, so inner can mean private.

clue.text: Opening of exhibition, flower festival

indicators.note: the opening of a word is where it begins, so only its initial letter is kept

blocks.note: the initial letter of exhibition
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: The first day of a big flower show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower festival' reads as one phrase, but the flower is wordplay and the festival is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival celebrating the resurrection of Jesus, held each spring.

clue.text: He initially rang one about freeloader

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of that word is kept
about can mean all around and turned over, so these letters are moved around

blocks.note: the initial letter of He
taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man phones someone to complain about a sponger.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger-on attaches themself to others for personal gain, living off them like a sponger.
